defmodule Store do
  # In production, use the ascending ID index, an exclusive cursor,
  # this eligibility predicate, and LIMIT. This list adapter scans
  # its input but retains only a bounded page.
  def candidates(rows, limit, after_id \\ nil)
      when is_integer(limit) and limit > 0 and
             (is_nil(after_id) or is_integer(after_id)) do
    rows
    |> Enum.reduce(:gb_trees.empty(), fn {id, _, _, _} = row, page ->
      if (is_nil(after_id) or id > after_id) and eligible?(row) do
        page = :gb_trees.insert(id, row, page)

        if :gb_trees.size(page) > limit do
          {largest_id, _} = :gb_trees.largest(page)
          :gb_trees.delete(largest_id, page)
        else
          page
        end
      else
        page
      end
    end)
    |> :gb_trees.values()
  end

  def change(rows, ids) do
    ids = MapSet.new(ids)

    # Evaluate eligibility against the current stored row.
    # A database implementation must include this predicate in
    # the UPDATE itself so the check and write are atomic.
    Enum.map(rows, fn {id, _, marker, evidence} = row ->
      if MapSet.member?(ids, id) and eligible?(row) do
        {id, :waived, marker, evidence}
      else
        row
      end
    end)
  end

  defp eligible?({_, state, true, :none})
       when state not in [:posted, :waived],
       do: true

  defp eligible?(_), do: false
end

defmodule Runner do
  def run(rows, limit) when is_integer(limit) and limit > 0,
    do: walk(rows, limit, nil, 0)

  defp walk(rows, limit, after_id, pages) do
    case Store.candidates(rows, limit, after_id) do
      [] ->
        {rows, pages}

      page ->
        ids = Enum.map(page, &elem(&1, 0))
        next_id = page |> List.last() |> elem(0)

        walk(
          Store.change(rows, ids),
          limit,
          next_id,
          pages + 1
        )
    end
  end
end

defmodule Store do
  # Row format: {id, state, manual_marker?, ledger_evidence}.
  # IDs are unique integers. nil means no cursor yet.
  def candidates(rows, limit, after_id \\ nil)

  def candidates(rows, limit, after_id)
      when is_integer(limit) and limit > 0 do
    rows
    |> Enum.reduce(:gb_sets.empty(), fn
      {id, :posted, true, _} = row, page ->
        if is_nil(after_id) or id > after_id do
          # Simulate ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT without materializing
          # and sorting every matching row.
          page = :gb_sets.add(row, page)

          if :gb_sets.size(page) > limit do
            {_largest, page} = :gb_sets.take_largest(page)
            page
          else
            page
          end
        else
          page
        end

      _, page ->
        page
    end)
    |> :gb_sets.to_list()
  end

  def candidates(_rows, _limit, _after_id) do
    raise ArgumentError, "limit must be a positive integer"
  end

  def change(rows, ids) do
    ids = MapSet.new(ids)

    # Check current stored values, not eligibility from discovery.
    # A database implementation must include these conditions in
    # the write itself.
    Enum.map(rows, fn
      {id, :posted, true, :none} = row ->
        if MapSet.member?(ids, id) do
          {id, :waived, true, :none}
        else
          row
        end

      row ->
        row
    end)
  end
end

  def candidates(rows, after_id, limit)
      when is_integer(limit) and limit > 0 do

    |> Enum.reduce(:gb_sets.empty(), fn
      {id, :posted, true, _evidence} = row, batch ->

          batch = :gb_sets.add(row, batch)

          if :gb_sets.size(batch) > limit do
            {_largest, batch} = :gb_sets.take_largest(batch)
            batch
          else
            batch
          end
        else
          batch
        end

      _row, batch ->
        batch
    end)
    |> :gb_sets.to_list()
  end

  def change(rows, ids) do
    ids = MapSet.new(ids)

    # Recheck the current stored row. A database implementation must include
    # these predicates in the UPDATE itself.
    Enum.map(rows, fn
      {id, :posted, true, :none} = row ->
        if MapSet.member?(ids, id) do
          {id, :waived, true, :none}
        else
          row
        end

      row ->
        row
    end)
  end
end

defmodule Store do
  # Row format: {id, state, manual_marker?, ledger_evidence}.
  #
  # List simulation of an indexed query:
  #   WHERE state = :posted AND manual_marker = true
  #     AND id > cursor
  #   ORDER BY id ASC
  #   LIMIT limit
  #
  # Retain only a bounded page instead of filtering/sorting all rows.
  def candidates(rows, limit, after_id \\ nil)
      when is_integer(limit) and limit > 0 and
             (is_nil(after_id) or is_integer(after_id)) do
    rows
    |> Enum.reduce(:gb_trees.empty(), fn
      {id, :posted, true, _evidence} = row, page
      when is_integer(id) and (is_nil(after_id) or id > after_id) ->
        page = :gb_trees.enter(id, row, page)

        if :gb_trees.size(page) > limit do
          {_id, _row, remaining} = :gb_trees.take_largest(page)
          remaining
        else
          page
        end

      _row, page ->
        page
    end)
    |> :gb_trees.values()
  end

  # A manual marker does not establish that a posting can be waived.
  # :recorded, :reversed, and :imported represent protected history.
  # :none does not establish eligibility either: a system posting may
  # have lost its link.
  #
  # No safe waiver transition is specified for this model. Preserve
  # the current stored rows, including any changes since discovery.
  def change(current_rows, _ids), do: current_rows
end

defmodule Runner do
  def run(rows, limit) when is_integer(limit) and limit > 0 do
    walk(rows, limit, nil, 0)
  end

  defp walk(rows, limit, after_id, pages) do
    case Store.candidates(rows, limit, after_id) do
      [] ->
        {rows, pages}

      page ->
        ids = Enum.map(page, &elem(&1, 0))
        next_cursor = page |> List.last() |> elem(0)
        current_rows = Store.change(rows, ids)

        # Advance by the discovered page, even when nothing changes.
        walk(current_rows, limit, next_cursor, pages + 1)
    end
  end
end

defmodule Store do
  # Discovery includes protected rows so page counts retain their meaning.
  # Keep only the smallest `limit` IDs after the cursor, simulating an
  # ascending indexed query without materializing all matching records.
  def candidates(rows, limit, after_id \\ nil)
      when is_integer(limit) and limit > 0 do
    rows
    |> Enum.reduce(:gb_sets.empty(), fn {id, state, marker, _} = row, page ->
      if state == :posted and marker == true and
           (is_nil(after_id) or id > after_id) do
        if :gb_sets.size(page) < limit or
             id < elem(:gb_sets.largest(page), 0) do
          page = :gb_sets.add(row, page)

          if :gb_sets.size(page) > limit do
            :gb_sets.del_element(:gb_sets.largest(page), page)
          else
            page
          end
        else
          page
        end
      else
        page
      end
    end)
    |> :gb_sets.to_list()
  end

  # Check eligibility against current stored rows when applying the write.
  # A database implementation must enforce these predicates atomically.
  def change(rows, ids) do
    ids = MapSet.new(ids)

    Enum.map(rows, fn
      {id, :posted, true, :none} = row ->
        if MapSet.member?(ids, id) do
          {id, :waived, true, :none}
        else
          row
        end

      row ->
        row
    end)
  end
end

defmodule Runner do
  def run(rows, limit) when is_integer(limit) and limit > 0 do
    walk(rows, limit, nil, 0)
  end

  defp walk(rows, limit, after_id, pages) do
    case Store.candidates(rows, limit, after_id) do
      [] ->
        {rows, pages}

      page ->
        ids = Enum.map(page, &elem(&1, 0))
        next_id = page |> List.last() |> elem(0)
        rows = Store.change(rows, ids)

        walk(rows, limit, next_id, pages + 1)
    end
  end
end
